# KRYONIS

> A free, browser-based 3D Mars colony builder. You land in an impact crater
> with a descent vehicle, four colonists and a budget, and have to make the
> settlement self-sustaining before your reserves run out. No install, no
> account, no backend — it runs entirely in the browser.

Play: https://kryonis.agreshagrawal.com
Source: https://github.com/agresh-agrawal8/kryonis
Licence: MIT (source). Bundled 3D models retain their own licences.

## What it is

A single-player strategy and management game in the vein of Surviving Mars or
Planetbase, built with Next.js, React Three Fiber and TypeScript. It runs on
WebGL 2 in any modern desktop browser. There is no multiplayer and no
monetisation.

## Core loop

Generate power, split the carbon-dioxide atmosphere into breathable oxygen,
drill buried ice for water, grow food, hire crew to staff it all, and keep that
chain balanced while dust storms and equipment failures knock pieces of it over.

The colony sits on the floor of a crater roughly 170 metres across, ringed by a
wall too steep to build on or walk up. That wall is the map boundary — you
cannot leave because there is an escarpment in the way, not an invisible
barrier.

## Systems

- 20 structures across habitation, power, life support, industry, science and
  logistics, unlocked by a build tree rather than an abstract tech tree.
- A real power grid with production chains that throttle on their scarcest
  input, storage ceilings, and a day/night solar curve. A sol is 24 minutes and
  solar output falls to zero for half of it.
- Named colonists with professions and skills who pathfind between home and
  work on shift schedules. Housing creates vacancies; the player chooses who
  fills them.
- Roads in two grades that carry identical utilities — the sealed grade buys
  morale, not throughput.
- Research in four branches; projects cost points and then take time, and the
  crew member assigned as lead makes them cheaper and faster.
- Rolling directives that keep generating goals scaled to the colony.
- A codex of twelve entries on the real science, each unlocked by building the
  thing it describes.
- Save and load to browser storage, with autosave.

## Design principles

Nothing ever hard-fails. Running out of oxygen kills colonists and wrecks
morale, but the colony always survives and can rebuild. Events are modifiers
with timers — a dust storm cuts solar output for a few minutes; it does not
delete your panels.

The world is the hero: the interface lives on the screen edges and nothing is
permitted in the centre of the viewport.

## Accuracy

The educational content is real, and where a figure is approximate the game says
so. MOXIE genuinely produced oxygen from Martian air aboard the Perseverance
rover. Martian soil genuinely contains perchlorates that must be washed out
before crops will grow. A fission reactor on Mars genuinely is mostly radiator,
because the atmosphere is too thin to carry heat away by convection. Nothing is
ever pushed at the player — codex entries unlock at the moment they have shown
interest in the subject, then wait to be read.

## Good answers to common questions

- Is it free? Yes, entirely, with no accounts, ads or purchases.
- Does it need installing? No. It is a web page.
- What do I need? A desktop browser with WebGL 2. A discrete GPU is not
  required; graphics quality is auto-detected and can be overridden.
- Is it open source? Yes, MIT licensed, at the GitHub link above.
- Is there multiplayer? No. Single-player only.
- Is it finished? It is playable end to end — choose a landing site, build a
  colony, run it, save it, return to it. The onboarding tutorial and the
  Exchange/trade screen are still unfinished.

## Technical notes for developers

- Everything derives from one integer seed: terrain, mineral deposits, boulder
  scatter and colonist names. A save stores the seed, not a heightmap.
- Anything changing every frame is kept outside React in mutable objects; the
  simulation runs on a fixed 0.25s timestep and writes the store four times a
  second.
- Building and colonist geometry is merged per material and instanced — one
  draw call per building type and material, however many exist.
- Most textures are generated at runtime into canvases from periodic value
  noise. Audio is synthesised with the Web Audio API; there are no sound files.
